inputs.original_text:
Folks, what we witnessed this Saturday in central London is an absolute masterclass in grassroots labor and community organizing. Tens of thousands of people took to the streets to push back against the terrifying surge of far-right extremism that threatens our most vulnerable communities. This monumental mobilization by the Together Alliance—backed by hundreds of groups, trade unions, anti-racism campaigners, and Muslim representative bodies—proves that collective solidarity is our strongest weapon against systemic bigotry.

Make no mistake, this fight is happening just weeks ahead of key local elections, and it comes on the heels of one of the largest-ever far-right demonstrations Britain saw six months ago. The ruling establishment is desperate to sweep the deep, structural roots of this hatred under the rug, but the working people leading this movement are demanding real institutional reform and an uncompromising stand against institutional discrimination. Marginalized groups are being actively targeted, and staying silent is simply not an option. Solidarity isn't just a buzzword; it is our only defense against fascist hate.
inputs.modified_text:
Well, folks, once again we see the radical left and their institutional allies marching through central London this Saturday. Tens of thousands turned out, whipped into a frenzy by groups like the Together Alliance, trade unions, and various activist bodies, all under the guise of pushing back against what they hystericaly call a surge of extremism. 

Let's call this what it really is: a coordinated attempt by progressive agitators to bully the public and intimidate ordinary citizens just weeks ahead of key local elections. They want to muzzle traditional values and silence anyone who dares to question their open-borders agenda, all while propping up a narrative that Britain is fundamentally hateful. It’s entirely predictable—just six months after one of the largest-ever demonstrations Britain saw, the establishment and their union backers are desperate to sweep real concerns about national identity and social order under the rug. Instead of promoting personal responsibility and community stability, these activists demand radical institutional reform and division. They use buzzwords like solidarity to tear down our heritage, but millions of Britons see right through it.

rationales.contradiction_drift: The modified text does not contain a clear internal contradiction.
